Typical clinical presentation: Asymmetrical, painless, non-tender lymph node enlargement (often >2 × 2 cm) for >1 month not responding to other treatment (e.g. antibiotics) With or without discharging sinus Most commonly cervical nodes a
Investigations: CXR Ultrasound (if available) Fine-needle aspiration biopsy or excision biopsy with histology, Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra, culture (if available) Respiratory specimens for Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra

Typical clinical presentation: Dullness on percussion and reduced breath sounds with or without pleuritic chest pain No acute illness
Investigations: CXR Ultrasound (if available) TST/IGRA Pleural tap with biochemical analysis and cell counts, Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra or culture (if available) b,c Respiratory specimens for Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra

Site of EPTB: Usually children aged <5 years with disseminated disease and severely ill

Typical clinical presentation: Subacute onset (>5 days) of headache, irritability or abnormal behaviour, vomiting (without diarrhoea), lethargy, reduced level of consciousness, convulsions, neck stiffness, bulging fontanelle, cranial nerve palsies
Investigations: CXR Lumbar puncture with biochemical analysis and cell counts and Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra (rather than culture initially) completed on CSF b Brain imaging (if available) Respiratory specimens for Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra TST/IGRA

Typical clinical presentation: Nonspecific symptoms with persistent fever, lethargy and wasting
Investigations: CXR (typical miliary pattern) Respiratory specimens for Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra Lumbar puncture with biochemical analysis and cell counts and Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra on CSF to exclude TBM b TST/IGRA

Typical clinical presentation: Abdominal swelling with ascites or abdominal masses No acute illness
Investigations: CXR Abdominal ultrasound Ascitic tap with biochemical analysis and cell counts, Xpert MTB/RIF, Xpert Ultra, or culture (if available) b Respiratory specimens for Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra

Typical clinical presentation: Deformity of spine, narrow-angle kyphosis (gibbus) May have lower-limb weakness, paralysis, or loss of bowel or bladder control
Investigations: X-ray spine Fine-needle aspiration biopsy or excision biopsy with histology and Xpert MTB/RIF, Ultra or culture (if available)

Typical clinical presentation: Cardiac failure Distant or muffled heart sounds Apex beat difficult to palpate
Investigations: CXR Cardiac ultrasound Pericardial tap with Xpert MTB/RIF, Xpert Ultra or culture (if available) b Respiratory specimens for Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra

Typical clinical presentation: Limitation of movement and abnormal gait Unilateral joint effusion (usually knee or hip) Swelling at end of long bones or small hand bones (dactylitis)
Investigations: Radiograph of joint or bone Joint tap or synovial biopsy, microscopy, Xpert MTB/RIF, Xpert Ultra or culture (if available) b Respiratory specimens for Xpert MTB/RIF or Ultra
